design: paired.  Each node is injected twice on the identical M >= 8 grid from a fresh default_rng(SEED): control keeps the frozen constant F_BINARY = 0.40, treatment applies the measured mass-dependent f_bin(M).  The per-star threshold consumes the same single rng.random(n_injected) draw in both arms, so donor, extinction, photometric and QMC realizations are bit-identical and the arms differ in exactly one thing: which stars got a companion.
why_paired: the published M >= 8 response is assembled from two files generated on different mass grids, so a grid-restricted re-run draws a different RNG stream even at the same seed.  Comparing the treatment directly against it would mix the multiplicity change with a change of Monte Carlo realization.
recovery_side_unchanged: both arms recover under the unchanged estimator, which keeps assuming 0.40.  That mismatch IS the bias under test.

f_bin_model.interpolation: linear in log mass, flat outside

V4_preflight.claim: adding truth_binary_fraction to inject_curve leaves the default path bit-identical

scope_limit: this is a DIAGNOSTIC.  It measures the size of the multiplicity effect on the WP6 closure ratio while holding accepted WP5 repair_v6 fixed.  Adopting a mass-dependent f_bin would also perturb the WP5 response inside 2-8 Msun through down-scatter from above, which requires a full repair_v7 chain re-run.  Masses below 8 Msun are deliberately not re-injected here.
